exceptions.reason: Today's core's Codex translator sends empty instructions on every Responses request; the extension sends the request's instructions as the client wrote them.

The new core sends the reasoning effort the client asked for (reasoning_effort, a Messages thinking budget's effort or a model-name suffix) whatever the model, and gives a translated request that names none the medium effort today's core gives it; today's core checks the effort against its model catalog and drops it for a model it does not list, such as gpt-test. The *-catalog-model cases and the codex-oauth cases show both cores sending it for a model today's core lists.

Today's core's Codex translator adds this default to every Responses request with tools (tool_choice, parallel_tool_calls, strict false, additionalProperties false); the extension sends the client's tools and choices as the client wrote them.

Today's core derives a session ID per conversation and sends it as prompt_cache_key; the extension has no session identity to derive from, so it sends only the client's own prompt_cache_key.
Today's core sends its session ID as the x-grok-conv-id header; the extension sends the header only when the client's body carries a prompt_cache_key, since it has no session identity of its own.
A non-streamed client gets a non-streamed upstream request, and its reply is read as one response; today's core always asks xAI for a stream and reads the stream into one reply.
Follows the request's stream flag (see the upstream stream exception); today's core always asks for an event stream.
The xAI extension names itself in its User-Agent (pluxy-xai and its version) and does not copy the Grok CLI's identity; today's core sends the Grok workspace's User-Agent unless the client sent one.
A Gemini function call names no ID; the new core makes a random one per request and today's core a counter. The ID only has to match the call and its output, and both do.
A Gemini function call names no ID; the new core makes a random one per request and today's core a counter. The ID only has to match the call and its output, and both do.

The new core writes the Gemini reply the same way for every upstream format: candidate index 0, the serving model in modelVersion, one chunk per text or thought delta, and a last chunk holding the finish reason, any function calls and usageMetadata (with Gemini's inclusion rules: promptTokenCount includes cached tokens, candidatesTokenCount leaves out thoughtsTokenCount). Today's Codex translator opens with an empty chunk, adds createTime and usageMetadata.trafficType PROVISIONED_THROUGHPUT, leaves out the candidate index and cached and thought token counts, names the requested model after the first chunk, and turns Responses encrypted reasoning into a thoughtSignature carrier on the next text part (Codex reasoning carry-over is the Codex provider's, slice 9); the new core reports the encrypted reasoning as dropped.
